source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Electrical-Body and Chassis, p.12-5

procedures.title: Headlamp aiming: checking that the floor is level
steps: (Continued) Turn each lamp vertical adjustment out until the bubble passes the black line on the vial, then turn clockwise to center the bubble between the lines.
With both bubbles centered, turn the car end for end, putting the tires back on the same floor spots.
If the bubbles stay within the two outer black marks, the floor is level enough to use the aimer as shipped.
If a bubble moves past the black lines, the floor slopes too much: try driving in at other angles, and if the bubbles still cannot be centered, calibrate for an unlevel floor.
Once a level spot is found, mark the tire positions on the floor for future use without calibration.
notes: For a quick level check, use the aimer (on its base pads) as a level with a straight 8 to 10 foot 2x4 laid where the wheels will be.

procedures.title: Headlamp aiming: calibrating aimers for an unlevel floor
steps: Do this for both aimers. Drive the car onto the area to be compensated and fit the aimers on the headlamps.
Loosen the knob under the aimer arm and move the slider until the bubble centers.
Note the numeral in the view window (used only for recalibration).
Set the slider halfway between that numeral and the "2" in the DOWN window (again only for recalibration, not aiming).
Turn the calibration screw (see figure 8 in the manual) until the bubble centers.
From now on aim only in this area with the car facing the same way; mark tire spots on the floor so other cars can be placed identically.

procedures.title: Headlamp housing (panel) alignment
steps: In-out: loosen the screws holding the slotted bracket to the underside of the headlamp housing and shift the housing.
Down: align the cover top to the opening by turning the hex head screw on top of the pivot link.
Open (actuator fully extended with rod): unhook the spring from the actuator rod pin...
